gallery.filename: Cotton Exchange Building, Union Avenue and Front Street, Memphis, TN (53699320910).jpg
gallery.title: File:Cotton Exchange Building, Union Avenue and Front Street, Memphis, TN (53699320910).jpg
gallery.artist: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
gallery.description: Built in 1922-1925, this Renaissance Revival-style skyscraper was designed by Mahan and Broadwell with C. G. Rosenplanter to house the Memphis Cotton Exchange, part of the cotton trading sector of the Memphis economy.  The building features a buff brick exterior, terra cotta trim, terra cotta spandrel panels on the principal facades, metal-frame windows, a terra cotta-clad base, arched transoms at the first floor bays, suspended canopies over the main entrance bays, decorative tapered doric pilasters, brick pilasters flanking the window bays on the principal facades with corinthian terra cotta capitals, and decorative reliefs.  Inside, the building features an intact lobby with a terrazzo floor, a ceiling with a decorative cornice, brass elevator doors with dial indicators flanked by reliefs of carved animal heads, marble-clad walls, and brass chandeliers.  The building is a contributing structure in the Cotton Row Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.  Today, the building houses various commercial office tenants, as well as the Cotton Museum of Memphis.

Photographs by Warren LeMay in Tennessee
